_about: The parity gate's configuration (tests/parity/compare.mjs). `gates` names what the gate holds: `full` routes are compared whole (landmarks by role and name, headings, controls, list containers and rows, row heights at 375); `frame` routes only for the shell the slice draws (frameControls, frameHeadings); `pixelExact` routes also gate on the 2 percent pixel diff; `lists` routes must have rows in their baseline. Every name in routes.json is gated or listed in `exempt` with a reason (gateProblems, tested). A gated route that is not compared is a FAIL unless `skippable` names it with a reason; the report ends `compared N of M gated routes`. `listEmpty` names a list route whose baseline account legitimately holds no rows. `approved` lists the differences from the baseline that a ruling allows, each with its ruling; nothing else may differ. It is empty because the baseline is the new production site (2026-10-19); a waiver must match a current difference, and the report ends with the `unused waivers:` line. `dataNames` kind `run` ({route, after, before, as, reason}) collapses the buttons drawn one per member between two anchor controls to one token on both sides. `conditional` ({route, match, reason}) names a control that exists only while some data does (an empty panel's Request coverage): compared when present on both sides, ignored when absent on either. `rulings` is text only.

exempt.reason: no baseline exists: the console is the platform admin's account data and the baseline job holds no admin sign-in. The deployed-preview capture (PARITY_ADMIN=1) still records it and its offences fail the compare; the layout is held at four widths by admin-smoke over populated mocks.

skippable.reason: baseline owed: the member account holds no group, so the capture finds no group page to discover (tests/parity/baseline/README.md). Capture it once the account joins a group, then delete this entry.

listEmpty.reason: the baseline account follows nothing (dash-search-smoke compares the empty state), so its list holds no rows; the rows are compared the day the account follows an item.

Artboard 16 draws 36 px auth fields (DESIGN CHANGES OWED 1); the artboard-01 privacy nav card rows are 44 px (pitch 46) where the artboard draws about 42 (OWED 10); the nav cap draws no band split while counts are unknown (rule 2 / INV-263, OWED 11). Retired with the same change: the single-main landmark (ASSEMBLY H.1, the shell supplies the one main), SEC-5 assignee names, tie-order and row-height waivers, and the settings, profile, market, research and map look waivers; each was a difference from the old site only.

V-9 (operator look ruling 2026-10-20): below 1440 px the rail folds under the content, so a list keeps its artboard width at 1280 (948 px beside the 252 px nav card) and the R1a title-column override is gone. The 1280 captures of the list routes change in layout only: the rail's controls and the rows are in the same DOM order with the same names, and compare reads no widths or positions (rows by name and order, heights at 375, pixels on four signed-out routes), so no difference arises and no waiver is written; the next baseline recapture shows the folded layout. DESIGN CHANGES OWED: artboards 04, 06 and 08 show the folded rail at 1280.

R2d (2026-10-20): the approved entries named r2d-* record three look/behaviour decisions the system ruled (rule 20): no jurisdiction is an em dash, the item type is words, and the market detail's Related corpus scan is removed. The neutral band for an unknown priority needs no entry: the compare reads no band colour and the tile counts compare as numbers (no unknown-priority row exists in the baseline account). Nothing else is waived. Second pass (2026-10-20, after 0090-0096 reached production): the entries named r2d-type-cut-*, r2d-period-start-*, r2d-lead-time-not-drawn, r2d-roadmap-copy-* and r2d-map-gap-link-name each cite the register row and, where an item is named, its id; every named item was read from production and is verified, current and unarchived.
